correctness.rationale: CDF power gives exact semigroup and negative-branch mass; conditional survival and its coupled exponential representation are algebraically exact, yielding monotone Weibull convergence. Each branch has one and only one strict log-density critical point because its derivative in powered distance is strictly decreasing with opposite endpoint signs. Implicit root expansions give the leading negative and positive modal positions; substitution in the exact density gives both height constants. A symbolic/numerical checker reproduces independent identities and twelve finite tests; analytical derivations cover the infinite ranges.

value.rationale: For a distribution marketed to model both extremes, the persistent two-mode density could misleadingly suggest two similarly substantial block-maximum regimes. This theorem supplies exact exponential extinction, a rare-event Weibull conditional shape, a monotone exact coupling, and sharp modal locations and heights; those specific quantitative facts explain what bimodality does and does not mean as block size grows, and are useful for interpreting extreme-risk fits.
